o1.biggest_strength: It makes the right core call fast: stop general blog work, shift capacity to comparison and cookie-related pages, and gives a concrete week-one task list the writer can start on Monday.
o1.biggest_mistake: It leaves too much upside on the table by prioritizing a /vs-google-analytics rewrite before the two no-page comparison terms, and one key statement is off: 46 trials per comparison page vs fewer than 1 per blog post overstates the blog gap because blog posts average about 0.7 trials per page.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the projections and page-ordering, add the explicit consolidate/redirect plan for decaying blog posts, and make the first-week tasks start with the two cheap wins the data points to: the cookie banner post and the without-cookies page.

o2.biggest_strength: It reads the data well, quantifies upside clearly, and gives a sensible month-by-month plan that stays mostly within capacity and keeps the brand constraints in view.
o2.biggest_mistake: It adds too much that was not earned by the brief: the GA4 rewrite forecast is too aggressive, it introduces new pages that may not match proven search demand, and it says to send the draft to the owner even though the brief says the owner is not available.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Cut the speculative pages, fix the over-optimistic traffic forecasts, and refocus the first 30 days on the highest-intent proven opportunities already in the data: missing comparison pages plus the two near-page-one cookie queries.

reason: Both saw the main pattern, but Output 1 is closer to something I would actually use tomorrow. It is more on-brand, more operational, and better respects the constraint that I want a real first-week plan without follow-up.
